title: Point epic_27_integration_lockout_redaction_atomic_test.dart AC3 at CompletionRepositoryImpl instead of a hand-rolled transaction
rule: TQ-8 (regression test must exercise the source; FR20 named invariant)

evidence.quote:
// production wire-up lives in `CompletionRepositoryImpl` (today the advance
  // is *outside* the transaction — DNI-385 ratifies the invariant the wire-up
// 6. Advance bookmark (outside transaction — uses content repo cache)

why: docs/planning/prd.md:563 states FR20 ("completion + bookmark update + points in single transaction"), and Story 27.9's own AC (docs/planning/epics-greenfield-rebuild.md:1548) says the bookmark advance is wired into the same transaction; epics.md:846 marks DNI-385 Done. But completion_repository_impl.dart awaits `_advanceBookmark` AFTER the transaction commits with no try/catch (lines 172-177) — if it throws, the completion is already persisted while the points-credit/analytics/milestone code later in the same `if (isNew)` block (lines 179-220) never runs, and the caller gets an uncaught exception. The acceptance test that is supposed to guard this never calls CompletionRepositoryImpl or BookmarkRepository at all; it hand-rolls its own db.transaction() wrapping a literal insert + throw, which only proves Drift's built-in rollback-on-throw, not the app's wiring — so a real regression (or, here, a real pre-existing gap) is invisible to this 'Done' story's own test. Confirmed empirically: `flutter test` on this file passes today regardless.
recommendation: Either wrap `_advanceBookmark` inside the same `_database.transaction()` in markComplete/bulk paths (if it's DB-only work) and update AC3 to call the real CompletionRepositoryImpl with a BookmarkRepository fake that throws, asserting the real completion-row count; or, if true atomicity isn't achievable (network/content-repo dependency), correct FR20/the Story 27.9 AC text and this test's claims to match reality instead of asserting a synthetic scenario.
acceptance_criteria: AC3 test constructs the real CompletionRepositoryImpl (or calls markComplete) with an injected BookmarkRepository fake that throws, and asserts on the actual persisted completion state.
Either production code wraps bookmark advance in the transaction, or FR20/Story 27.9's AC text is corrected to state the actual (non-atomic) behavior.
